question: What religious obligations does a severely autistic or special needs child have?
asked: I have a child who is on the extreme side of the autistic spectrum, severely autistic. What should I do Islamically in terms of obligations on her? It's a female child. I love her immensely. I want her to go to Jannah, so I want to do my best to make sure that she gets there.
answer:
Autistic child, or let's just make it broader: any child with special needs, any child that is a special needs child, intellectually, and even physically. This will be covered here.

First and foremost, dear mother and dear parents: Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala has chosen to gift a special needs child to you, because it is a gift from Allah. Realize that with this gift there is also a different type of struggle and a different type of test. And like all of us have specific trials and tests and gifts and blessings, so too a child with special needs: it is a gift and a special type of test. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala gives special tests to special people.

Our Prophet ﷺ said, and this is a famous hadith, all of you should know it: when Allah loves a group of people, He will give them special tests. The bala', the ibtila' will come for special categories of people. And there is no question that a child that requires more love, and more tenderness, and more concern, and more care, for a much longer period than other children, there is no question that this is a special, blessed struggle that you have, that other people can only imagine, can only think about.

And our Prophet ﷺ said, and the hadith is in Tirmidhi, that the greatness of the reward comes with the greatness of the struggle. The more was the love, the struggle, the tenderness, the more effort you had to put, the more will be your ajr with Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

So I remind you, dear sister, and also dear father and mother, all of you, and anybody who has any issue in life that they're struggling with: I remind you that Allah says that every sabir person, Allah will give them back their ajr without even counting. So this is going to be the test of your motherly and fatherly love that you will continue to give.

Most other children, after a while, become semi-independent, and then they become fully independent, and then we become dependent on them. This is the cycle of life; that is the default. But perhaps in some special needs cases, the child will never become fully independent, and the parents will continue to give and give and give. So realize that as you give, Allah will give back to you. Realize that your ajr is dependent upon your own sabr and your own iman. And indeed Allah 'azza wa jall has only put you in this situation because Allah knows you can overcome it, and Allah has chosen to raise your ranks high in Jannah for your efforts.

And so put in that effort, expecting the reward from Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. If our Prophet ﷺ reminded us that even a thorn prick will forgive the sins, even the slightest nuisance will forgive sins, what do you think about having to wake up every single day, extra effort for the child, having to feed, having to do this and that? If a thorn prick is going to bring our jaza' in Jannah, what do you think of love that is shown to another human being, to a son or a daughter that has special needs?

So realize that Allah 'azza wa jall has indeed chosen you for something that is a test and a trial at some level, but it is a test and a trial that is meant to increase your barakah. In the hadith in Musnad Imam Ahmad, the Prophet ﷺ said: whenever Allah tests His servant with something and he is content, radi, then Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala will give him barakah and increase what he has. And if he is not content, Allah will take away from him even more and will not give him barakah.

Now I want to say something, dear parents who are tested with this issue. I swear to you: you are being tested in one way, yet Allah has blessed you in other ways. This is from the hadith: if Allah has taken something away from anyone, then Allah will give him something else that he might not even recognize. It'll be in his face, but the love that will come, or the rahmah that will come, or the sakinah that will come, or the positive that will come from another aspect of his or her life, will be something that is gifted because of the difficulties that they are in. And that's exactly what Allah says:

> فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
> إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا

And it is through people like you that we, the rest of us who are not tested with these struggles, we see the reality of love, and motherly love, and rahmah. Yesterday we had a guest over; those of you that were here, we saw an amazing example of prophetic forgiveness still walking on this earth. We saw something that touched our hearts, when the father forgives the murder of his own son for the sake of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. What a moving testimony. So subhanAllah, you see these living examples.

Then guess what, dear mother, dear father: you become a role model for your family and friends. They will look at you and they will say, "SubhanAllah, look at that person's iman and taqwa." You might not feel you have iman and taqwa, and you should not feel that you are, but others look at you, and others will be inspired by your dedication. For in ways you don't even know, you will become a role model, subhanAllah, and their good deeds will be given to you, and they will also have good deeds.

In other words, when you are taken as a role model, when somebody does a good deed because of you, Allah will bless the first person, and Allah will bless you as well, that you are the one who inspired that person. So when you become a positive role model through your sabr, through your patience, you will become somebody who will get deeds without even recognizing and knowing it until Judgment Day. And there are reports in the hadith that people will be rewarded and they'll be like, "Where did this come from?" And it will be because of the effects of their good deeds. So this is the first issue.

Also, by the way, realize that our Prophet ﷺ showed great kindness to all, and he showed especially kindness to children and to those who were special needs. There is a hadith in Sahih Bukhari. Anas ibn Malik narrates: there was a lady who was mentally challenged in the life of the Prophet. Obviously every society has people like this. She wasn't normal, and she walked up to the Prophet and she said, "Ya Rasulallah, I have something very important I need to talk with you about." There is nothing important. She's not going to be protecting against an army; it's in her mind. She's mentally challenged, right? And she wants to have a session privately: "I want to take you away, and I want to have something very important."

So our Prophet, and everybody knows she is mentally challenged, everybody knows, and subhanAllah, maybe me or somebody else would be like, "Okay, maybe another day, I just have no time." This is the way we are. But he is Rasulullah ﷺ. Even though there cannot be anything important that she has to ask or say, he said to her, "Ya amat Allah, O lady servant of Allah, fine. Where do you want me to talk? Take me to any place and we will go talk." So she took him to some corner over there, and Anas said: we saw her talking with him until he resolved her issue, and then he came back. SubhanAllah, this is rahmatan lil-'alamin.

Whatever she had, for sure, it's in her mind; it's something trivial. And I say this, and wallahi I feel guilty that I'm not able to even do a fraction of this, even though I'm saying the hadith. May Allah forgive me for any shortcomings, and all of us. This was a lady who didn't even have a genuine need, and she was mentally challenged. So if anybody has an excuse to say, "Who has time for you? I have to solve the problems of the Ummah," it should be our Prophet ﷺ. But he said, "Ya amat Allah, where do you want to have a conversation? Take me anywhere." And she took him to that corner street. And Anas said that it was in the sikak al-Madinah, just another alleyway. And whatever the issue was, whatever was in her mind, the Prophet ﷺ spoke with her and then came back. SubhanAllah. So the mercy and compassion and tenderness should be there.

Now, your question, dear mother, was one that really touched me. SubhanAllah, honestly, the email was so beautiful. You did not complain; you did not say, "Why am I tested with this?" Rather you said, "I love my daughter, I want her to go to Jannah." What a motherly love is this, subhanAllah. "I want to make sure that I'm doing everything..." The question was more detailed, about prayer and whatnot, and she's an autistic child, so obviously you understand that it's not going to be the same thing here. So she's worried that the child is not necessarily fulfilling all of the obligations. I did not know the age of the child, but I'm assuming maybe 14, 15, 16, because she's worried that the child is not doing the regular things of Islam. So the mother is saying: what is my responsibility to this child?

So to answer this part of the question, I say to you that in our Shari'ah, Allah is indeed arham al-rahimin. Wa la yukallifullahu nafsan illa wus'aha. And realize that by unanimous consensus of all the scholars of Islam, the one who is mentally incapable, the one who is mentally challenged, the obligations are lifted from them. **The one who is not able to think critically at all has zero obligations, and this is unanimous consensus.**

Reported in Abu Dawud, our Prophet ﷺ said: three people the Qalam has been lifted from, meaning no hisab, no 'adhab, nothing will happen to them. The Qalam has been lifted from them:

1. Number one, the one who is asleep. Whatever he does in his sleep, he's not sinful if he falls down and accidentally...
2. Number two, the saghir, the child. Accidentally the child might flip a button, something happens; the child is forgiven.
3. And number three, the majnun, the one who doesn't have 'aql, until he gets his 'aql back.

So there is no responsibility on the majnun. In Arabic, "no taklif" is the term; taklif is legal burdening, or legal responsibility.

And in the famous incident of the one who committed zina and confessed to the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ wants to get rid of him, because he didn't want to punish him; he wants to forgive him. So he asked him a series of questions, and one of the questions, he asked somebody else: "Is this man known to be majnun?" Meaning, if he was known to be majnun, then I have nothing to do; if he drank, if he did something, it's not my business, let him go away. So he asked, "Is he known to be crazy? Is he mentally incapable?" Which means that the Qalam has been lifted from him if he was mentally incapable.

And as for the issue of the Akhirah as well, Ibn Hazm says in his al-Fisal: as for the majnun who cannot think rationally until they pass away, then they shall be like children, following the parents' religion. They shall be like children who follow the religion of the parents. So if their parents were believers, then they will be considered believers, and they will die in a state of iman, and they will be of the people of Jannah. So this is the position of Ibn Hazm, and it is a logical one as well, that it's not their responsibility to be thinking in this way.

Now, you are asking to what level of responsibility, and I say: nobody can answer this other than you. Realize, the more the child or the young man or girl is able to think, the more taklif comes on them, and the less they're able to think rationally, the less taklif is on them. So it's directly proportional: the more they're able to think, the more responsibility comes.

Only you know. Does your son or daughter understand the time? Does your son or daughter understand how to break and make wudu, what breaks wudu? Only you understand. And there are autistic people that maybe cannot communicate properly, but they're super geniuses other than this, and they can understand everything, but they have a problem communicating. And so they can pray, and they can fast, and they can do wudu, but they're socially awkward; they don't know how to speak the way we are accustomed to speaking. And then there are those on the more extreme side that cannot think rationally the way they are. Maybe they are 15 years younger intellectually, so instead of being 30 they're 15, or whatever it is.

Nobody knows other than you, and therefore **you be the judge in this regard, and err on the side of mercy and caution.** Err on the side of mercy and caution. And you are allowed to test them: "Okay, is it time for salah or not?" See if they understand or not. And if they're intellectually able to understand the time, and they're able to do the salah, then you encourage them without being harsh, because at the end of the day, their framework is different than ours, and their understanding is different than ours.

So I'm not saying let go completely, but I'm also definitely saying: don't treat them with any degree of harshness or strictness. Treat them the way that Allah 'azza wa jall would want them to be treated, which is with rahmah and mercy, and Allah 'azza wa jall will reward you for all that you have done, and you will get the ajr for this. So this is the first issue. I cannot answer it explicitly, simply because nobody knows to what level of taklif other than you. But err on the side of caution.
